schema.name: AuroraBot
schema.description: An open-source autonomous-agent framework for an Agent with a life of its own.

hero.title: An Agent with a life
hero.description: AuroraBot is an open-source autonomous-agent runtime. She keeps sensing her environment and thinking and working in her own rhythm. Your messages matter, but they are one kind of change in the world around her.
hero.processAria: How AuroraBot handles a change in the environment
hero.eventDescription: Messages, time, application events, and action receipts enter through one boundary.
hero.contextDescription: Changes are grouped by session, then a fast or root Agent triages them with memory, Tasks, and permissions.
hero.decisionDescription: Models, tools, and delegation all create Activities; only results from the current generation may commit.

philosophy.title: Conversation is only part of the environment.
philosophy.description: AuroraBot does not treat a chat window as the center of the world. She has persistent state, unfinished work, and her own rhythm, and she treats changes from people, time, applications, and other Agents on equal terms.
philosophy.lifeTitle: She has a life of her own
philosophy.lifeDescription: Time and work continue when no message arrives. An active rhythm lets the Agent decide, within a budget, whether a moment calls for thought or action.
philosophy.equalityDescription: A user message does not automatically become the highest command. The Agent understands the event before choosing to respond, delegate, act, or stay quiet.
philosophy.controlDescription: The model judges. External action passes through capability authorization, argument validation, and Platform execution before its outcome returns to the causal chain.
philosophy.capabilitySummary: This design gives AuroraBot continuing Tasks, multi-Agent collaboration, replaceable models, MCP capabilities, Platform composition, persistent state, and causal records. They serve one goal: helping an Agent do more than chat, so she can live reliably in an environment over time.

ways.title: Multiple ways to connect.
ways.description: Console, Panel, and MCP / headless offer distinct entry points, while Agents use the same cognition-and-action loop through every one.
ways.consoleDescription: The shortest path for direct interaction, status queries, development, and debugging.
ways.panelDescription: The core repository provides a loopback, single-owner backend for accounts, sessions, chat, and WebSocket; the complete browser UI is a separate project.
ways.mcpDescription: Connect external capabilities through MCP, or compose AuroraBot into your own environment without a local interface.

start.title: Run from source.
start.description: You need Python 3.12 (recommended; higher versions are not fully verified), Git, uv, and the API key required by the default model configuration.
start.installComment: # Fetch the project and install runtime dependencies
start.configComment: # Add DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; disable Aurora-QQ in config/apps.toml if it is not installed
start.runComment: # Start the Console and default MCP Platform
start.previewDescription: Suited to local exploration, runtime research, and extension development. Degradable long-term memory is available; complete attachment understanding, sandbox and speech runtime support, stable MCP reconnect, data TTL and consistent backup, and public multi-tenant guarantees are not.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions.
faq.differenceQuestion: How is AuroraBot different from a regular chatbot?
faq.differenceAnswer: AuroraBot treats chat as part of the environment, not all of it. She also manages an active rhythm, continuing Tasks, Agent collaboration, and receipts from external actions.
faq.equalityQuestion: Does treating messages equally mean ignoring the user?
faq.equalityAnswer: No. Interactive Tasks can still receive scheduling priority. Equality means a message is understood as an event before it becomes a response, action, delegation, or deliberate silence—not that it becomes an unquestionable system command.
faq.memoryAnswer: Yes. Short-term windows and summaries, global durable facts, and mem0/Chroma semantic retrieval are in the runtime. If semantic retrieval is unavailable, memory falls back to keyword search over durable facts.
faq.modelsAnswer: Fast, quality, multimodal, and embedding roles map to Providers through TOML. Current conversational calls use Chat Completions semantics, with tool definitions and fallback based on model capabilities.
faq.toolsQuestion: How do I add my own tools?
faq.toolsAnswer: Implement a stdio or HTTPS Streamable HTTP MCP Server, declare its connection in apps.toml, then authorize Tool IDs or wildcard patterns in agents.toml. Arguments are validated against the Server schema, and outcomes return to the causal chain as tool receipts.
faq.panelQuestion: Is Panel a complete web application?
faq.panelAnswer: This repository only contains the loopback, single-owner local backend and chat bridge. The complete browser UI is maintained in AuroraBot-panel; Console remains the shortest path to try AuroraBot.
